messages:
sam (support): FYI urgent: BrightDoc is seeing intermittent 504s from hosted API for a high-traffic route. Customer reports ~10% of requests getting timeouts and p95 jumping to 2.3s around 11:02 UTC. They attached traces.
kevin (sre): Thanks Sam — can you paste the sample request IDs and tenant id? Also any correlation ids from their traces?
sam (support): tenant=brightdoc-prod, sample request_id=req_3a7f22, req_3a7f88, req_3a7f99. They said it started after a spike at ~11:00 UTC after a marketing campaign.
maria (oncall): I'm on it. Kicking off quick checks: ingress metrics, gateway queue depth, and continuous-batcher backlog.
maria (oncall): ingress-bot please dump recent gateway queue metrics for tenant=brightdoc-prod for 10:50-11:10 UTC.
ingress-bot: metrics dump started for tenant=brightdoc-prod (10:50-11:10) — returning summarized counters: gateway.request.count=128k, gateway.5xx.count=1.2k, gateway.queue_depth.p95=980, gateway.queue_limit=config(1000), batcher.backlog_ms.p95=1250ms, kvcache.evictions=4200.
kevin (sre): queue_depth p95 at 980 while limit is 1000. That’s dangerously close. batcher backlog ~1.25s p95 suggests continuous batcher is accumulating work at the tail. Looks like burst pushed us to soft limit and some requests timed out waiting in the gateway.
sam (support): Customer reports many of the 504s are tail-timeouts, not immediate rejects. They see retries from client but still poor UX.
nina (eng-runtime): Possible causes: long KV cache misses causing slower token generation for a subset of requests, or batching window increased due to low throughput which delays small requests. Any model version change?
maria (oncall): No model rollouts at that time. Quick grep of deploy bot logs: deploy-bot: no model deploys between 10:30-11:30 UTC.
deploy-bot: no active rollouts found.
kevin (sre): Can we get runtime p50/p95 per-request generation time and per-token times around 11:00? Also continuous-batcher queue length distribution.
ingress-bot: runtime metrics: model.gen_time.p50=80ms, p95=420ms, tokens.per_request.avg=64. continuous_batcher.queue_len.p50=12, p95=140, queue_len.max=1024. Note: queue_len.max > gateway.queue_limit because batcher buffers across workers.
nina (eng-runtime): queue_len.max=1024 is bad — we have internal buffering exceeding gateway limits. That explains tail latency: some requests sit in internal batcher queue longer than gateway will wait for. Also see kvcache.evictions spiking — KV cache misses may be forcing extra compute per request.
maria (oncall): Root hypothesis: sudden tenant spike overloaded batching pipes and KV cache thrash increased per-request latency => queue accumulation => gateway tail-timeouts as requests sat waiting.
sam (support): Customer wants mitigation now — what can we do immediately?
kevin (sre): Short-term mitigations (fast):
- Increase gateway queue_limit for brightdoc-prod to 1500 for next 30m to reduce early rejects (risk: memory usage).
- Temporarily pin brightdoc-prod to a lower-latency model variant (smaller quantized) that reduces gen_time p95.
- Throttle or shed background low-priority routes for that tenant (if they have non-critical endpoints).
- Force batcher to use preemption: lower max-batch-size and increase concurrency for that tenant.
Pick one or two.
nina (eng-runtime): I can push a small change to batcher config to reduce batch window from 25ms -> 12ms and increase per-worker concurrency by 1. That should drop backlog but increase compute cost. I can also enable KV cache pinning heuristic for BrightDoc to reduce evictions if they have repeated contexts.
maria (oncall): Kevin, can you bump gateway queue_limit for tenant to 1500 for 20m? I can coordinate runtime config changes.
kevin (sre): Doing it now: `POST /admin/tenants/brightdoc-prod/config` payload `{ "gateway_queue_limit": 1500, "temporary": true, "ttl": 1200 }` — applied. Confirming metric update...
ingress-bot: gateway.queue_limit for brightdoc-prod updated to 1500 (applied by kevin)
maria (oncall): Nina, please apply batcher tuning.
nina (eng-runtime): Applying batcher change to tenant routing group brightdoc-prod: 
```
PATCH /runtime/config
{ "tenant": "brightdoc-prod", "batcher_window_ms": 12, "batcher_concurrency_add": 1 }
```
Applying...
deploy-bot: runtime config rollout started for brightdoc-prod (canary 10%)
kevin (sre): After ingress bump and batcher patch, watch for queue_len.p95 and gateway.5xx.
ingress-bot: metric snapshot 11:08 UTC (post-mitigation): gateway.queue_depth.p95=320, batcher.backlog_ms.p95=210ms, gateway.5xx.count delta=+12 (down from +1.2k), request.success.rate improved.
sam (support): Customer confirms error rate dropped and UX improved. They still see occasional slow tails but much better. They want a postmortem and permanent fix.
maria (oncall): For the postmortem and permanent fixes:
- Fix mismatch between internal batcher max buffer and gateway queue_limit — enforce consistent global soft limits or propagate backpressure to gateway earlier.
- Add tenant-level adaptive preemption: when a tenant's queue_len crosses X% of gateway limit, reduce batch window and increase concurrency automatically.
- Improve KV cache TTL heuristics to avoid mass evictions during traffic spikes (or increase cache memory for heavy tenants).
- Add an operator-visible tenant throttling control in Console to allow support to instant-throttle noisy tenants.
nina (eng-runtime): Agree. Also propose adding a per-tenant admission controller: if internal backlog > gateway_limit, start applying per-request priority and early-fail non-critical requests (soft-fail with 429 or lower-cost fallback model).
kevin (sre): Action items:
- kevin: add a temporary dashboard showing internal batcher queue vs gateway limit per-tenant (ETA 2h).
- nina: PR for auto-preemptive batcher tuning + KV cache heuristics (ETA 1d).
- maria: postmortem draft (ETA 4h) with timeline and customer-impact note.
- sam: follow up with BrightDoc and offer runbook for traffic spike mitigation + SRE support for next campaign.
sam (support): I'll loop in customer and schedule a call. Thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
maria (oncall): Leaving notes here for postmortem: timeline, mitigations applied, metrics before/after, and proposed config changes. Will tag ownership and runbook steps.
kevin (sre): Quick repro steps for engineering to reproduce in staging:
1) Simulate tenant traffic spike: `wrk` with parallel connections to route with similar tokens/request distribution (payloads with variable KV hits).
2) Reduce model workers by 20% to mimic resource constraint.
3) Measure continuous_batcher.queue_len and gateway.wait_time until backlog grows > 80% of gateway limit.
4) Verify tail-latency timeouts and reproduce 504 patterns.
(Include scripts in the incident doc).
ninga (typobot): (typo detected in previous message: 'ninga' should be 'nina')
kevin (sre): Closing note: mitigation verified, customer recovered. Moving to postmortem and long-term fixes. If any new 5xx spikes reappear, escalate to oncall immediately.
sam (support): Filed follow-up ticket with BrightDoc contact and scheduled postmortem call for 16:00 UTC. Thread archived after final notes.
